explanation.text: Ultrafiltration is pressure-driven movement through a selective barrier, not active transport of each solute. Small molecules enter the capsule filtrate while blood cells and most plasma proteins remain in the capillary.

reasoningChain: Explain the hydrostatic pressure and barrier structure.
Identify substances that pass and substances that are retained.

stem.text: Caffeine is a natural compound present in tea and coffee. Caffeine is also added to some drinks. Some people produce more urine after having a drink containing caffeine than after drinking an equivalent volume of water.
Suggest ways in which caffeine may cause an increase in urine production in some people.

points.text: idea that less / no, ADH binds to receptors (at the collecting duct) ;
ref. to fewer / no, aquaporins, in / added to, membranes (of cells in collecting duct) ;
ref. to less water reabsorbed (at collecting ducts) ;
increase in blood pressure so increase, in GFR / volume of glomerular filtrate ;

markScheme.note: Point n follows the order of the transcribed marking points; table rows or source labels such as 3a and 3b retain their original wording.

explanation.text: More urine can result from greater filtration or reduced reabsorption. Changes in ADH action affect collecting-duct water permeability, whereas changes in glomerular pressure affect filtrate formation.

reasoningChain: Consider filtration and water reabsorption separately.
Suggest mechanisms that increase urine output in the stated direction.
